summary: Phase 2 In-App Notifications & Activity Log tested end-to-end. BACKEND: 13/14 PASS in /app/backend/tests/test_notifications.py (covers list/sort/limit, unread-count, mark-read for specific ids/null/empty/idempotent, triggers for auth.login/auth.lockout/user.created/user.reactivated/stock_master.created/stock_master.deleted, and visibility rules for staff). FRONTEND: NotificationBell fully verified — bell visible in topbar, badge='3' after admin login, dropdown opens with 18 items (correct icons, colors, timeAgo, title, message), click an item decrements badge (3→2), Mark-all-read clears all and disables itself, click-outside closes dropdown, all data-testids present. ONE BACKEND BUG: DELETE /api/users/{id} does NOT fire any notification — spec requires audience=admin, type=user.deactivated. The endpoint at server.py L636-645 (deactivate_user) is missing the _notify(...) call entirely, so admins never see user-deletion events in their feed.

critical.issue: Missing notification trigger. Spec requires _notify(type='user.deactivated', audience='admin') on soft-delete, but the deactivate_user handler (server.py L636-645) only updates is_active=false and returns {ok:true} — no _notify call. As a result admins never see user-deactivation events in the activity feed. Note: PUT /api/users/{id} with is_active=false DOES correctly emit user.deactivated (L619-626), so a workaround is to use PUT, but the DELETE trigger spec'd in the requirements is broken.

critical_code_review_comments: _notif_visibility_filter (server.py L654-668): clean and correct — admins get {} (everything), staff get $or of audience=user+target_user_id OR audience=module+module∈allowed. audience='admin' rows are correctly invisible to staff. ✅
_notify (server.py L131-165) correctly swallows exceptions so a notification failure can never break the underlying business operation. ✅
BUG (HIGH): deactivate_user (DELETE /users/{id}, L636-645) is missing the _notify call — inconsistent with the matching PUT path at L619-626. Spec explicitly lists this trigger.
GET /api/notifications applies visibility filter twice — once for items, once for unread count (L696 + L700). For better DRY/perf, compute the filter once and reuse. Minor; not blocking.
MarkReadRequest treats both `ids=None` and `ids=[]` as 'mark all visible'. This matches the spec ('with {ids:null} or {ids:[]} marks ALL'). Verified in tests. ✅
NotificationBell.jsx polls every 30s + on window focus, properly cleans up listeners on unmount, and uses click-outside via mousedown — all correct patterns. ✅
_notif_to_public correctly excludes Mongo `_id` (already excluded by find projection {_id:0} on L699). ✅

The X-Unread-Count response header is set on GET /notifications and exposed via Access-Control-Expose-Headers (L701-702) — nice touch for cheap polling, but the frontend currently doesn't use it (it parses the JSON body instead). Either remove the header or wire it into a HEAD-style endpoint to save bandwidth.

rca_of_the_issue: Bug: DELETE /api/users/{id} doesn't emit user.deactivated notification. Reproduction: (1) Login admin; (2) POST /api/users to create a user; (3) DELETE /api/users/{id}; (4) GET /api/notifications — there is NO row with type='user.deactivated' for that user_id. Direct cause: deactivate_user() at server.py L636-645 only does db.users.update_one(...is_active:false...) and returns {ok:True} without ever calling _notify(). The PUT update_user() handler does emit the notification (L619-626) when is_active flips. Mitigation: Append a _notify(actor=admin, type='user.deactivated', title='User deactivated', message=f\"{admin.get('email')} deactivated {target.get('email')}.\", audience='admin', ref_collection='users', ref_id=user_id) call at the bottom of deactivate_user, right before `return {ok: True, deactivated: True}`. After fix, re-run pytest backend/tests/test_notifications.py to confirm 14/14.
